Negligence

NEG-lih-jens — contains 'neglect'; negligence is the state of neglecting your duty. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Negligence is failure to take the proper care owed to people or things in your charge.

The factory was shut down after inspectors found dangerous negligence in how chemicals were stored.

Worked Example

A daycare worker leaves toddlers unsupervised near a pool for twenty minutes while checking her phone in another room. Thankfully nothing happens, but a parent later discovers what occurred and is furious.

Failing to give proper care and attention when it was clearly required is negligence. Unlike 'mistake,' which can be a harmless slip, negligence specifically means failing in a duty to be careful.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

neglect: Neglect is the ongoing failure to look after someone or something in your care — a garden, a pet, a duty left untended over time. Negligence is the legal-sounding cousin: a specific failure to take the care you owed, often judged from a single incident.

oversight: An oversight is an honest miss — a detail nobody noticed or a step nobody remembered, often through simple carelessness. Negligence is heavier: it means a real duty of care existed and was not met, which is why oversights are forgiven and negligence can be punished.

dereliction: Dereliction is the willful abandonment of a duty — a guard who walks away from the post on purpose. Negligence does not require intent at all: it is failing to take proper care, even through pure inattention, when the duty was yours.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

diligence: careful and persistent effort or attention

vigilance: careful attention to possible danger

Where it sits · how badly proper caution is ignored — carelessness → negligence → recklessness

carelessness vs. negligence: Carelessness is a milder relative of negligence — a careless mistake is minor and often harmless, while negligence implies a real failure of duty that can cause serious harm.

recklessness vs. negligence: Recklessness is stronger than negligence: negligence is a failure to take proper care, but recklessness means knowingly ignoring an obvious danger.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — neg-

Prefix — neg-: not (Latin)

Root — lig

Root — lig: to pick, to choose, to gather (from Latin legere, 'to pick up, to choose')

Suffix — -ence

Suffix — -ence: state or quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Neg- ('not') + lig ('to pick, to choose, to gather' — from Latin legere) + -ence ('state or quality of'): Latin neglegere combined neg- (not) with legere (to pick up, to attend to). Negligence is, at its root, a failure to 'pick up' or attend to something that needed care.

Use the root in a new word: eligible

Use the root in a new word: eligible: Only students with a certain grade point average are eligible to apply for the scholarship.
